body.statement: For every nonempty branch \(\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\), finite linear-program duality gives \(L_{a,b}^r(P)=V_{L,a,b}^r(P)\) and \(U_{a,b}^r(P)=V_{U,a,b}^r(P)\), with attaining unrestricted multipliers in \(\mathbb R_+^2\). Combined with Theorem 1, these values give the sharp exact-support arm-mean closure. At \(P^\star\) for \(a=1\) and \(r=\mathrm{SDC}\), \(\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P^\star)=[711/1100,911/1100]\subsetneq\mathcal I_{BK}^\star=[0.496024,0.872824]\), so the theorem strictly tightens the published normalized outer union at a legal full-support law.
body.justification: The unrestricted cone is the intrinsic LP dual, and the rational example makes the correction empirically nonvacuous.
body.gap: BanKedagni2022 normalizes the multiplier magnitude and states validity without sharpness; earlier cone discussion does not supply endpoint duality or the support filter. KédagniLiMourifie2018 Theorem 2 gives an equivalent unit-sphere characterization for its finite zero-covariance model, whereas this theorem dualizes the two-inequality SDC sign cone and combines it with the positive-slack support filter; for arbitrary finite \(h\), the two moment classes overlap but are not generally nested.
body.consumer: Applied users obtain exact population endpoints and a certificate showing when the published outer region is unnecessarily wide.
